name: Victoria

seo.title: Landscaping in Victoria, BC: Gardens & Stratas | RNC
seo.description: Garden care, courtyard planting, irrigation and tree work for Victoria homes and stratas, with the City tree bylaw checked before we prune. Get a free quote.

cardSummary: Compact heritage gardens, shaded strata courtyards and downtown frontages, with many trees protected by City bylaw.
intro: Many Victoria gardens are compact and long established: heritage lots in Rockland and Fairfield, shaded courtyards in Fernwood, apartment stratas in James Bay and downtown frontages where every bed is on show.

Mature trees are the common thread. The City protects many of them, including Garry oak and arbutus from 50 cm tall and trees on steep slopes or near watercourses, so pruning, removals and digging in a root zone start with a bylaw check. Browse [tree and vegetation work](/services/tree-vegetation/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/?area=victoria).
localRulesIntro: The City of Victoria has its own tree bylaw with low thresholds for native species and hedges, on top of the regional watering and invasive-plant rules. Hedges count too: one stem over 30 cm can bring a hedge under the bylaw.

localNotes.title: Victoria Tree Protection Bylaw
localNotes.text: Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw protects private trees over 30 cm diameter at breast height, hedges with any stem over 30 cm, Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific yew and Pacific dogwood over 50 cm tall, replacement trees, and trees on steep slopes or near watercourses. A permit may be needed to prune, remove or work in the root zone of a protected tree.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Wind and salt along the Dallas Road shore
conditions.body: Gardens in James Bay and south Fairfield face the Strait of Juan de Fuca and take winter wind and salt spray. Tough, wind-tolerant shrubs and grasses usually outlast soft-leaved plants there.

conditions.title: Shade and roots on mature lots
conditions.body: Big street and backyard trees in Fairfield, Rockland and Oaklands shade lawns and compete for water. Lawns often thin out under them, and shade-tolerant beds or mulch can be a better use of the space.

conditions.title: Rock close to the surface
conditions.body: Some lots, especially around Rockland and the city’s rocky knolls, have bedrock close to the surface. Shallow rock changes what can be dug, so it is worth probing before planning a patio or new beds.

conditions.title: Regional water on every lot
conditions.body: Victoria properties are on the regional supply, so the CRD lawn days apply. Stratas water on the complex’s street address, not each unit’s.

topServices.why: Small lots and strata courtyards need regular, tidy visits more than big projects, and compact beds show neglect quickly.
With hedges and native trees protected at small sizes, most tree jobs here begin with a check of the City’s bylaw.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Weekly and every-other-week care for compact city lawns, boulevard-facing beds and strata courtyards.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Planting plans for tight city lots and shaded courtyards, built around protected trees.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Controllers set to the CRD lawn days for your address, including a complex's street address for stratas.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Pruning and removals with a check of Victoria's Tree Protection Bylaw first.

jobNotes.title: Corner-lot hedge cut back from the sidewalk
jobNotes.body: A corner hedge was trimmed back to clear the sidewalk sightline, after confirming no stem was large enough to bring it under the bylaw, and the bed behind it was replanted with low, drought-tolerant shrubs.

jobNotes.title: Courtyard drip split by sun and shade
jobNotes.body: An apartment strata’s single drip zone was split in two so the shaded north beds stopped staying wet while the sunny south beds dried out.

cta.heading: Get a free quote for your Victoria property
cta.body: Tell us the neighbourhood and what is growing there. If a large tree or hedge is involved, mention it so the bylaw check is part of the plan.
